I am testing the Dell 32-inch UltraSharp U3226Q, and so far the impressions are excellent. The picture quality of this OLED panel is stunning, especially when HDR is enabled on macOS. I will be releasing a full UltraSharp review video on my YouTube channel.

I want to specifically mention an important improvement Apple has made to HDR support in macOS 27. When using a third-party HDR-capable display with macOS 26 Tahoe, there was a drawback: you could not enable HDR at the popular 2560 x 1440 scaled resolution. Fortunately, the latest version of macOS has resolved this issue.

The Problem

If you are using a third-party HDR10-capable display with macOS Tahoe, you can see the HDR toggle in Settings → Displays. Once enabled, you can view HDR content. You can see this situation in the screenshot below.

But note in the same screenshot, my display is running at a resolution of 1920 x 1080, which is 2x pixel scaling of this 4K UHD display's native 3840 x 2160 resolution.

Most users would probably not want to use 1920 x 1080, as content looks far too large on a 4K display. The Dell UltraSharp U3226Q is a 32-inch display, so using 1920 x 1080 significantly reduces the amount of visible screen space.

Solving this issue in macOS is simple — just select a scaled resolution, such as the popular 2560 x 1440, which is the default setting for the Apple 5K Studio Display. The problem is that after selecting a scaled resolution in macOS Tahoe, HDR gets disabled. Note the screenshot below:

As you can see, the HDR toggle has disappeared, and macOS automatically reverts to SDR. In other words, to use an HDR display with macOS Tahoe, you must choose between HDR and your preferred scaled resolution.

Fortunately, this issue has been fixed in macOS 27 Golden Gate. As you can see in the screenshot below, scaled resolution and HDR can now be enabled simultaneously — you can have both. This is a native system option and does not involve any third-party software.

So if you are using a third-party HDR display, this feature alone is worth upgrading from macOS Tahoe to macOS Golden Gate, in my personal opinion. Of course, I am using an M4 MacBook Pro. I also tried the same operation on an M1 Max MacBook Pro, but even running macOS 27, I was unable to select both settings simultaneously, so it appears there are hardware requirements.

macOS Golden Gate includes many new features, which I have covered in my Siri AI overview, macOS highlight features video, and final macOS 27 review. One feature related to HDR displays is that macOS 27 provides more comprehensive native HDR support at the system level.

Compared to macOS Tahoe, you will notice that specular highlights and cursors are brighter, and overall contrast is significantly improved. Whether you are using an Apple Studio Display XDR, Pro Display XDR, or a third-party OLED display, you can get an exceptional viewing experience.

What do you think? Would you use a third-party external display with a Mac? If so, would you consider using an HDR-capable display?
